name: Kon Tum Wooden Church
summary: Walk the timber cathedral on Nguyen Hue, cà chít wood raised from 1913 to 1918 with Roman arches under a Ba Na roof. Entry is free and an hour covers it. If Ba Na village life is what you came for, give the time to Kon K’Tu instead, about 5 km out across the Kon Klor bridge.
getThere: Walk from central hotels on Nguyen Hue
heroCaption: The timber façade and spire on Nguyen Hue

notice.title: Sunday Mass fills the nave
notice.body: Mass is at 6:00, 8:00, and 17:00 on Sunday. Come between services for a quiet look at the timber.

body: The cathedral stands on Nguyen Hue in Thống Nhất ward, built from 1913 to 1918 in dark cà chít timber. The arches are Roman and the roof is Ba Na. Step inside for the stained glass, the timber columns, and the carved sanctuary.

An hour is enough. Come in the morning, after a two-bowl phở near the market, and keep the afternoon for the river. Kon K’Tu is a different visit: a Ba Na village about 5 km out, across the Kon Klor bridge, that takes two to three hours.

figures.caption: The nave and sanctuary inside the wooden church
figures.alt: Timber columns, stained glass, and the sanctuary inside Kon Tum Wooden Church

gettingThere: The church is on Nguyen Hue in Thống Nhất ward, in the centre of town. Walk from any hotel in the centre. From Pleiku Airport, the bus or taxi into Kon Tum takes about an hour.

legs.heading: From Pleiku Airport (PXU)
legs.body: About an hour by bus or taxi to the centre: nearly 45 km by kontumtourism.com’s count, 51 km by Travelmath’s. Then walk.

hours: Sunday Mass at 6:00, 8:00, and 17:00. Visitor hours outside Mass: Check on arrival.
